newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Budapest run sets pace for E.Europe bourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Budapest run sets pace for E.Europe bourses.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange continued to outpace other regional bourses with a record-breaking run this week, while fears crept in elsewhere that heavy flooding might dampen spirits in coming months.
Shares in Warsaw, Bucharest and Bratislava also gained ground. But Czech and Slovenian equities slipped and in Croatia volumes were thin and prices mixed.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest Stock Exchange watched a six-session string of closing highs halted on Thursday by a one percent correction but analysts remained bullish on the bourse's outlook for coming weeks.
The BUX index closed on Thursday at 7,219.2, a rise of some 70.17 points over the course of the week.

Gaspar Czako, an analyst at Eastbrokers, said the market's fall on Thursday did not come as a surprise. "This is a technical correction...which could be expected as the market ran away a little bit," Czako said.
But dealers saw no reason for the long-term upward trend to break, though another correction might come.
PRAGUE

Czech shares edged lower over the course of the week after a sharp rise last Friday, pushed down by concern over the economy, especially after torrential rains left nearly one-third of the country flooded, closing many major factories.

Dealers said data showing another contraction in industrial output in May was more bad news for a market reeling from poor economic fundamentals that have helped turned investor attention to other bourses in the region.

"Heavy flooding in parts of the country could also damage the economy, though it is still early to tell how much, which could hurt fundamentals even further," said Boris Gomez of ING Barings. "At this point, we just have to wait and see."
Added one regional analyst in London: "We are really concerned. Poland, the Czechs, Slovakia, they all may see share prices fall in some sectors because of plant closures."
WARSAW

Polish shares rose 2.3 percent this week to 15,933.6 points but analysts saw a fall on Friday and a flatter market next week despite Thursday's high turnover caused by strong demand for copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA.
KGHM started trade at 23.5 zlotys ($7.1) on Thursday, 11.9 percent above its institutional-investor issue price.

"The recent growth was likely linked with hopes that money invested in KGHM would return to the market, which has probably happened to a degree," said Dariusz Szepieniec, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
"But it seems the extra demand was too short-term and small to lift prices significantly," he added.
Analysts said large-cap KGHM might still have some upside potential despite its relatively high market ratios.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) saw another week of listless trading, with brokers expecting this situation to last at least over the summer.
The official 16-share SAX index, however, managed to eke out a slight gain on some blue chip advances, closing at 169.7 on Thursday, 0.2 points above Monday's opening.

Brokers said they saw some signs of revival in investors' interest but did not expect liquidity to increase in the near future. "It's hard to match a deal on this illiquid market at the moment," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
BUCHAREST
Most Bucharest prices moved ahead under stronger buying pressure in second tier issues as investors started looking at cheaper, smaller capitalisation stocks.

Romania's failure to win inclusion in the first wave of NATO expansion at the Madrid summit was ignored by investors as operators said foreigners were more interested in Romania's advance with its tough reforms.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks traded mixed as volume and turnover dwindled with buyers taking a break. Market participants expected trade to remain directionless for a while.
"Summer is here and there is nothing to pull the market up. I cannot see any reversal for a week or two," said one trader at a large bank.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 1.99 percent this week, as the blue-chip SBI index dropped 29.08 points to 1,431.02.
But market participants forecast that the index was likely to rise by about 20 percent over the summer with foreign capital flows showing no signs of slowing.
Traders said foreign investors, mostly regarded as long-term buyers, would continue buying even if parliament fails to ratify a European Union association agreement before July 15.
